root_cause.text: The IPv4 IP options parsing code in `ip_options_get()` did not enforce capability checks when unprivileged users set Source Route Record (SRR) options (IPOPT_SSRR and IPOPT_LSRR), allowing any application to manipulate packet routing paths.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a capability check `if (opt->opt.srr && !ns_capable(net->user_ns, CAP_NET_RAW))` that was previously absent in the `ip_options_get()` function. The vulnerability existed since Linux 2.6.12-rc2 (commit 1da177e4c3f4), indicating that SRR options were never restricted to privileged users. This allowed unprivileged applications to force packets through attacker-controlled nodes to leak TCP ISN and other protocol information, as described in the CVE.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add capability check to prevent unprivileged users from setting IP source route options, enforcing CAP_NET_RAW requirement for this sensitive network operation.
intent_record.what: Added a new conditional check after line 532 that validates whether the caller has CAP_NET_RAW capability in the network namespace when the ip_options structure contains a source route record (srr) option. If the check fails, the function frees the allocated opt structure and returns -EPERM error code.
intent_record.how: This change adds a security boundary that prevents unprivileged users from setting IP source route options. At runtime, when ip_options_get() is called with source routing enabled, the kernel now verifies the caller's capabilities before accepting the options. If the caller lacks CAP_NET_RAW in their network namespace, the operation is rejected with a permission error, and allocated memory is properly cleaned up.
